correctness.rationale: Normalize the scalar quartic quotient on a compact fourth-power sphere. Euler homogeneity identifies the Lagrange multiplier with the positive quotient at a maximizing nonconstant triple. The subtracted Lagrange equations show every all-distinct stationary triple has zero sum and quotient \(9\). A repeated common coordinate equal to zero gives quotient \(2\); otherwise scaling reduces to \(f(t)=2(1-t)^4/(2+t^4)\), whose derivative is \(8(t-1)^3(t^3+2)/(t^4+2)^2\), so its global maximum is \((1+\sqrt[3]{2})^3\). Summing the resulting scalar inequality coordinatewise gives the upper bound for arbitrary \(\ell_4(I)\), while the explicit three-coordinate cyclic unit vectors attain equality. Quantifiers, normalization, the dimension restriction, and the equality case are explicit; no finite sampling is used as proof.

value.rationale: \(J_T\) was introduced to quantify three-point geometry of Banach unit spheres; \(\ell_p\) spaces are the canonical benchmark family. The result gives a sharp, dimension-stable exact value for the first even non-Hilbert exponent beyond \(p=2\), supported by a reusable sharp scalar quartic inequality and a complete equality construction. It is not a mere renaming, parameter substitution, or table recomputation, and the exact value can serve as a benchmark for inequalities relating \(J_T\) to classical geometric constants.
